Free State death roads

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Free state roads have become death traps - the network is at a tipping point as Citizens take on politicians

Unique Selling Point:
Footage of appalling roads and accidents that were entirely preventable
great case studies and a lot of angry people and stats of money wasted that makes your hair stand on end

Summary:
Free state roads across the province are crumbling. There have been 25 deaths in 4 months on the R30. On the R34 a teacher died when he hit a pothole. Trucks have fallen down embankments - Contractors have ripped R830 million from the department but the roads are still broken. 280 contractors are in a legal battle with the department. William Bulwane former MEC for Agriculture is trying to fix the problem but his critics say he is useless. And the farmers and the locals are fuming. So much so they have taken to blocking roads in protests - we have all these visuals
On Tuesday the 31 May the premier is going to inspect a road where a video has just gone viral - and give a press conference - we will go and film it - but the board of Free State Agriculture are so mad with the situation that they are calling for Bulwane's head and are delivering an MOU to the premier demanding she gets a more competent MEC.

Further information:
We speak to the farmers, the politicians, the headmasters who send busloads of children up and down these death roads and the agricultural businesses who can no longer operate effectively as the country's farming province loses its valuable road network

Extra Budget Items:
Petrol and Travel - the R3 50 doesnt even touch sides and there is a lot of travelling - we will probably only stay over one night - too dangerous to travel on the roads at night

Case Study:
Henk Botha

Expert:
Mr. jack Armor

Free State

Script:


Free State Death Roads FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX SUNDAY 19th JUNE 2022

Voice over 1
For a while now, we had received reports about the hazards of Free State roads, so we took a journey that began on the R34 close to the Bloemhof dam in the West of the Province

Then another to meet farmers on the R30 that carries traffic through the provinces centre

And a hair raising drive close to the provincial border in the East where the R34 continues into Northern KZN

And on each road we discovered how ineptitude and indifference by the provincial Roads department had led to injuries and death

fade to black

Voice over 2
On the last day of May, an icy wind blows across the R34, as journalists await the Premier’s arrival

Trucks travelling

She was coming to inspect the state of this road that had embarrassed her officials when a truck driver filmed his journey – and this video went viral.

Truck driver
“This is how people have to drive on these roads, every which way, in the middle, next to the road- you can’t even drive next to the road anymore. How ridiculous is this?!

Voice over 3
The truck driver lambasted the Free State ANC for destroying the roads, mocking the politicians blue light brigades. He has a point - The Free State premier doesn’t travel light

Blue light arrival

And her inspection of the road with MEC William Bulwane, was confined only to the first potholes of the 12 kilometre stretch in the truckers video – conveniently leaving out the far more embarrassing section

Premier
I understand and I am not happy because these smallanyana potholes by tomorrow the department should start working on them

Voice over 4
But these are not smallanyana potholes, this is complete disintegration of an important economic link.

Free State Agriculture’s Dr. Jack Armour took us for a bumpy tour

Dr Jack Armour in car
The 34 is quite a major road that links the whole of the Free State linking a lot of important agricultural towns, but the R34 goes all the way to Richards Bay- and I am sure this is a manganese truck going past us right now

LINK
It’s fair to say that the road network in the Free State is at a tipping point. The question is, can the premier and her MEC bring them back from the brink?

Voice over 5
Seven months ago, MEC William Bulwane moved from Agriculture to Police, roads and transport. If the road network gets worse, he’s the politician to blame.

MEC Bulwane
Most of the roads in the Free State, their lifespan have lapsed so they have aged they need to be redone.

Voice over 6
But he has neither the R20 billion rand nor the skills his department requires. Right now there aren’t even enough grader operators. His former MEC outsourced maintenance to inexperienced contractors – costing R736 million rand over 3 years with little to show for it.

MEC Bulwane
We don’t do this shady works. I want to leave a legacy myself so I want my legacy to be on these roads

Voice over 7
George Michalakis represents the Free State in the National council of Provinces on behalf of the DA. He has been probing where and how roads money is spent

George
Now the irony is that the provincial department sits with road authorities that is tasked with building the roads – they are underfunded or they have a top heavy funding where office personnel receive massive salaries but they don’t employ people on the ground that can actually do the work. So you have a department just taking salaries – you are not funding them to do their work and you are contracting this out to contractors who don’t have a clue how to build the roads. And that is the crux of the problem.

Link
This is the R30, it’s an important link for farmers and the mines, but it’s become a point of tension – here in the heart of the Free State

Voice over 8
February brought heavy rains and flooding, over a section of the road.

More than 25 people have died. Some drowned when a bus, taxi and cars aqua-planed into the water

There were 50 accidents so MEC Bulwane just closed the road, but that had a devastating effect on the local farmers because they couldn’t get their grain to the silo’s

Rudi Jansen Van Vuuren is a local farmer

Mac
Why is the anger to Free State roads department?
Rudi
We felt from the beginning they weren’t doing enough to fix the problem. The road was just closed, when we complained they opened it, I think in total it was opened and closed about eight to ten times, that the road was open and closed open and closed and our problem is now the alternative route is being driven

Voice over 9
The alternative route is this 18 kilometer backroad which the farmers maintain at their own expense. Suddenly it was carrying mining trucks moving at high speed and slow moving farm vehicles. That caused further accidents

Crash, crash, crash

In May, fed up farmers blocked the road for an hour to make their point to government.

Rudi
We felt that we had reached a deadlock with the roads administration and we felt they didn’t hear us

Voice over 10
The road level of the flooded R30 was then raised by a private company at their own expense with permission from the province, and it was reopened.

Jack looks at debris

But Dr. Jack Armour who liaises with more than 3000 farmers and the province, says what came next was just as dangerous

Bulwane’s department erected sand barriers to try and stop drivers accessing the road, but with insufficient signage that couldn’t be seen at night

It was an accident waiting to happen

Car crashes into the sand wall.



Dr Jack Armour
So one can understand the concern of government that this road is really dangerous, but from our perspective the government hasn’t done enough to alert to the dangers of this perfectly safe road if travelers were just alerted to slow down, to be aware, to take it slow

Voice over 11
But now Free State roads wants to build a bridge here

Dr Jack Armour
The farmers clearly don’t trust government. What is government going to do with the money why do they want to build such an expensive bridge – looking for any excuse to build massive infrastructure skim off the top from

Voice over 12
When we arrived last week – fuming farmers and local townspeople waited patiently for the premier and MEC Bulwane

Cars roll in

Voice over 13
Three hours late - the premier, a phalanx of MEC’s and a local mayor arrived. The travelling extravaganza had come to Alan ridge – and crossed the sand barrier that by now, stopped no-one including the premier’s entourage

Premier
Hi How are you?
Uys
We have a huge problem here you know

Voice over 14
The farmers came straight to the point

Uys Van Heerden
We can’t just stop an economy and say close the road. We can’t close the road!

Voice over 15
To her credit – the premier diffused the volatile gathering

Premier
We know that without you the economy of the Free State is nothing that is why we have decided that we must meet with you, because you are very important

Voice over 16
The premier reminded the farmers that every death is a claim against their department
And she set up a task team meeting with her officials and farmers



Premier
What you are saying we can hear it. We don’t want to lose the economy but we also don’t want to lose people’s lives

Voice over 17
Our final stop was in the Eastern Free state on the R34 punctuated with potholes and sadness

Truck roars up the hill

It links the small towns of the Free State to Northern Natal.

Last year, a teacher driving a school bus had just dropped off children, and was returning to his school in Vrede – but he never arrived.

The school bus hit a pothole, the tyre had a blow out and the bus veered headlong into a truck. Three people died that day.

Henk Botha is the principal of Vrede High and primary school

Henk Botha
I couldn’t believe it, it was indescribable, one doesn’t want to relive it. Your brain doesn’t want to process it

Voice over 18
After the accident he wrote a letter begging Free State authorities to please fix the roads

Mac
Did you ever get a response to that
Henk
Nothing! Nothing! To this day nothing. How many more must die before something is done to these roads?

Voice over 19
That same question has been asked by another principal, 60 kilometres south east of Vrede in the small town of Memel

Up sound Netball

Johann Du Toit is a both a principal and a paramedic, and is first responder at horrific accidents on these Free State Roads

Mac
When you arrive at a scene what is the first thing that goes through your mind?
Johann
Anger, Anger. Just imagine yourself getting there and you see bodies lying there and its due to potholes

Mac
In any of these accident were there children, because for me sometimes that is the worst?

Johann teary
Yes definitely, breaking limbs, falling out of cars, seeing them under the space blanket, the little feet- seven or eight years old

Voice over 20
Here there have been no blue light road shows – in fact no shows from anyone who can fix a road. Tar is thin, patchy and dangerous

Johann
Look at the thickness of that!

Voice over 21
There were 4 accidents here in 12 days in December. Nothing was done, then a few weeks ago two trucks collided and fell into the vlei spilling oil and coal

Johann
the other one couldn’t brake fast enough and it seemed like the two trucks hooked and they both went down into the vlei due to the same potholes which I have begged them to please go and fix, five months before

Voice over 22
With around 3000 damaged tyres and a mounting death toll, locals in Memel decided they had to end the carnage themselves. Drikkie Coetzee is a Newcastle teacher that moved to Memel.

Drikkie Coetzee
I came here and everyone was complaining and I thought let’s just nudge this in some direction

Voice over 23
It began with only five tonnes of tar scrounged from the roads department, and snowballed from there

Now a Newcastle businessman has contributed equipment, local labour is paid for by farmers and residents, and together they are fixing these provincial roads without a cent coming from the Free State budget

Johann
We got a phone call from a person from Vrede in the roads department that we need permission to work on the roads. I don’t think at this stage I have to ask anyone to save lives we will do what is necessary to save lives – and if it is to fill potholes that is what we will do that

Voice over 24
So is this what it’s come to? Citizens scrounging tar to fix the Free state’s roads at their own expense? And what of MEC Bulwane’s legacy -to complete these roads by 2024

Bulwane
We are going to do our level best, we may not finish them but we will attempt to finish them

Voice over 25
Just this week, another vehicle slammed into the sand barrier on the R30, and farmers with a few provincial workers and their own, urgently constructed rumble strips – hoping to rescue their local economy, and most importantly, save lives

THE END 12 13

PROMO ONE 11 seconds
The Free State road network is at a tipping point – now fed up locals are fighting back

Uys Van Heerden
We can’t just stop an economy and say close the road. We can’t close the road!

PROMO TWO
Free State provincial authorities failed to fix dangerous potholes, so locals did it themselves

Johann
We got a phone call from a person from Vrede in the roads department that we need permission to work on the roads. I don’t think at this stage I have to ask anyone to save lives

PROMO THREE
V.O
Free State’s roads are crumbling
MEC
Most of our roads in the Free state their lifespan have lapsed
VO
So much so that motorists are getting injured and killed on roads that have seen little maintenance for years
Henk
How many more must die before something is done to these roads?
VO
Now the new MEC of roads and transport must find a solution

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Free state roads have become death traps - the network is at a tipping point as Citizens take on politicians
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Footage of appalling roads and accidents that were entirely preventable great case studies and a lot of angry people and stats of money wasted that makes your hair stand on end
metadata.Summary: Free state roads across the province are crumbling. There have been 25 deaths in 4 months on the R30. On the R34 a teacher died when he hit a pothole. Trucks have fallen down embankments - Contractors have ripped R830 million from the department but the roads are still broken. 280 contractors are in a legal battle with the department. William Bulwane former MEC for Agriculture is trying to fix the problem but his critics say he is useless. And the farmers and the locals are fuming. So much so they have taken to blocking roads in protests - we have all these visuals On Tuesday the 31 May the premier is going to inspect a road where a video has just gone viral - and give a press conference - we will go and film it - but the board of Free State Agriculture are so mad with the situation that they are calling for Bulwane's head and are delivering an MOU to the premier demanding she gets a more competent MEC.
metadata.Further information: We speak to the farmers, the politicians, the headmasters who send busloads of children up and down these death roads and the agricultural businesses who can no longer operate effectively as the country's farming province loses its valuable road network
